targetWords.definition: To admire someone is to like them for what they do.
targetWords.example: I admire my brother for his hard work.

targetWords.definition: To aid someone is to help them when they need something.
targetWords.example: The doctor aided the boy after his accident.

targetWords.definition: To attempt something is to try to do that thing.
targetWords.example: I am attempting to learn English.

targetWords.definition: Authority is the power that someone has because of their position.
targetWords.example: The policeman has authority on the streets.

targetWords.definition: A capital is an important city where a country's leaders live and work.
targetWords.example: • \Ne will visit the capital to learn about our government.

targetWords.definition: To cooperate is to work together to do something.
targetWords.example: The students cooperated to clean up the classroom.

targetWords.definition: To defend someone or something is to protect them from attack.
targetWords.example: The soldiers defended the town from the invaders.

targetWords.definition: Destruction is damage to something so bad that it can't be fixed.
targetWords.example: After the big fire, there was much destruction in the city.

targetWords.phonetic: d i s o r d e r
targetWords.definition: Disorder is a lack of order, or a complete mess.
targetWords.example: ■The teacher's desk had many papers in disorder.

targetWords.definition: A division is the act of making smaller groups out of a larger one.
targetWords.example: The chart had six divisions which all had different colors.

targetWords.definition: To enable a person is to make it possible for them to do something.
targetWords.example: Having the key enabled us to open the door.

targetWords.definition: To frustrate is to prevent someone from fulfilling their desire.
targetWords.example: • The machine frustrated me because I could not fix it.

targetWords.definition: To govern is to control the public business of a country, state, or city.
targetWords.example: The United States is governed from the White House.

targetWords.definition: To have plenty of something is to have more than you need.
targetWords.example: The school had plenty of books for the students to read.

targetWords.definition: To relieve someone is to make them feel less pain.
targetWords.example: The medicine relieved the sick boy.

targetWords.definition: Reputation is the opinion that people have about someone.
targetWords.example: The doctor had a reputation for helping people.

targetWords.definition: Royal describes something that belongs to a king or queen.
targetWords.example: The king sat upon the royal throne.

targetWords.definition: A slave is a person who is not free and must work for someone else.
targetWords.example: The slave worked very hard all day long.

targetWords.definition: — The kids struggled with each other for the toy.
When someone is stupid, they lack intelligence.
targetWords.example: He said something stupid that made everyone angry at him.

story.title: The Tale of Bartelby O'Boyle
story.passage:
Long ago, there was a clever man by the name of Bartelby O'Boyle. As a boy,

he was kept as a slave by the royal family. He saw other children play, but he

always had to work. This frustrated him very much. But he was not stupid, and

he wanted to change things.

Then one day there was a struggle for authority in the kingdom. There was a

division of the people, and one group fought against another group to see which

would govern the kingdom. There was disorder in the kingdom. Bartelby ran

away. He saw much fighting and destruction. Many

people had nothing to eat; Bartelby decided to aid

them. He would help them get food. But how?

Bartelby went to the capital to find
